text:
Evan Rodrigues came to New Jersey with two Stanley Cup rings from Florida and the label of a veteran presence. Twenty-four games later he has seven goals and 13 points, The Hockey News has called him a secret weapon, and Sheldon Keefe has said he's exceeded expectations.

The hot streak is partly earned. He has eight points in his last ten, and his own chances are up (2.4 expected goals against 1.9 usual). But seven goals on 4.3 expected means 19% shooting after 7% last season, and that rate rarely lasts. The two kinds of luck pull against each other: the Devils have scored 5.4 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice, so the assists should pick up even as the goals slow. At five on five his line is about even (51%), nearly seven points worse than without him on a dominant team. He breaks out cleanly, 64% of exits with possession in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. Undrafted out of Boston University. Our range projects 32 to 49 points.
